In [[algebraic topology]], a branch of mathematics, the '''based path space''' <math>PX</math> of a [[pointed space]] <math>(X, *)</math> is the space that consists of all maps <math>f</math> from the interval <math>I = [0, 1]</math> to ''X'' such that <math>f(0) = *</math>, called based [[Path (topology)|paths]].<ref name="fiber sequence">Martin Frankland, [https://uregina.ca/~franklam/Math527/Math527_0304.pdf Math 527 - Homotopy Theory - Fiber sequences]</ref> In other words, it is the [[mapping space]] from <math>(I, 0)</math> to <math>(X, *)</math>.

A space <math>X^I</math> of all maps from <math>I</math> to ''X'', with no distinguished point for the start of the paths, is called the '''free path space''' of ''X.''<ref>{{harvnb|Davis|Kirk|2001|loc=Definition 6.14.}}</ref> The maps from <math>I</math> to ''X'' are called free paths. The path space <math>PX</math> is then the pullback of <math>X^I \to X, \, \chi \mapsto \chi(0)</math> along <math>* \hookrightarrow X</math>.<ref name="fiber sequence" />

The natural map <math>PX \to X, \, \chi \to \chi(1)</math> is a fibration called the [[path space fibration]].<ref>{{harvnb|Davis|Kirk|2001|loc=Theorem 6.15. 2.}}</ref>
